rules.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance just cause eviction requirement
rules.requirement: To evict a tenant from a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have one of 17 enumerated just cause reasons, and that reason must be the dominant motive for the eviction. Expiration of a lease or a change in ownership is not just cause. A just cause reason is also needed to remove housing services such as parking, storage, or laundry, except for temporary removal for mandatory soft-story seismic retrofit work under Section 37.2(r).
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental units covered by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance. This includes some tenancies exempt from the Ordinance's rent increase limits, such as newly constructed units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979, tenancies eligible for rent increases under Costa-Hawkins, and some tenancies whose rent is regulated by another government agency.
rules.exemptions: Units not covered by the Rent Ordinance. The document does not list the specific exemptions.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Unit must be covered by the Rent Ordinance's eviction provisions. Coverage of some government-regulated tenancies varies.

rules.penalty: Landlords who evict or try to evict unlawfully may face substantial civil and/or criminal liability.
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction. Note that the mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership does not constitute "just cause" for eviction.
